definitions.explanation: An optical phenomenon where light bends through layers of air at different temperatures, creating the appearance of distant objects being displaced or inverted, or the illusion of water in deserts.

examples.japanese: {砂漠|さばく}で{蜃気楼|しんきろう}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw a mirage in the desert.

examples.japanese: {富山湾|とやまわん}は{蜃気楼|しんきろう}の{名所|めいしょ}として{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Toyama Bay is famous as a spot for viewing mirages.

examples.japanese: あの{計画|けいかく}は{蜃気楼|しんきろう}のように{消|き}えた。
examples.english: That plan vanished like a mirage.

notes:
KANJI ORIGIN:
・{蜃|しん} (giant clam) + {気|き} (vapor) + {楼|ろう} (tower)
・Ancient Chinese believed giant clams breathed out vapor that formed phantom towers
・This mythology gave the phenomenon its name

TYPES:
・{上位|じょうい}{蜃気楼|しんきろう} (superior mirage - objects appear elevated)
・{下位|かい}{蜃気楼|しんきろう} (inferior mirage - objects appear below actual position)
・{逃|に}げ{水|みず} (road mirage - appearance of water on hot roads)

FAMOUS VIEWING SPOTS IN JAPAN:
・{富山県|とやまけん}{魚津市|うおづし} (Uozu, Toyama) - most famous
・Spring (April-May) is best viewing season
・{蜃気楼|しんきろう}ロード (Mirage Road) is a designated viewing area

SCIENTIFIC CAUSE:
・Temperature difference between air layers
・Light refraction creates distorted images

FIGURATIVE USE:
・Something illusory or unattainable
・{蜃気楼|しんきろう}のような{夢|ゆめ} (an illusory dream)
